Hyperbole and a Half

Allie Brosh

Hyperbole and a Half

Touchstone/Simon & Schuster

Allie Brosh is the mind behind the enormously popular blog Hyperbole and a Half, which receives millions of unique visitors a month. This amalgamation of new material and reader favorites from Brosh’s blog includes stories about her rambunctious childhood; the highs and mostly lows of owning a smart, neurotic dog and a mentally challenged one; and moving, honest, and darkly comic essays tackling her struggles with depression and anxiety, among other anecdotes from Brosh’s life.

Annotation: Hyperbole and a Half is a collection of stories about depression, anxiety, identity, and Brosh’s dogs (helper dog and simple dog). Originally posted as a webcomic , the stories have been collected, although in a different order, for this book. Several parts take on heavy topics – such as depression – in a lighthearted way. Around the bits about mental health are incredibly funny things her dogs have done and explorations into her life as a child. The art is intentionally simplistic for comedic effect.

The Anatomy of Hyperbole and a Half: A Cultural and Journalistic Reckoning

Hyperbole and a Half, at first glance, present

...

the book’s core thesis crystallized: that hyperbole, far from being mere rhetorical flourish, is a survival mechanism; a way to compress the unbearable weight of lived experience into digestible, resonant forms.
This is not a simple defense of exaggeration. Moreci argues, with meticulous self-scrutiny, that hyperbole functions as both shield and scalpel: it distorts enough to protect the self, yet sharpens enough to reveal deeper truths. The book’s title, borrowed from a line in a forgotten self-help axiom, encapsulates this paradox—“half” referring not to half-truths, but to the uneven balance between fact and feeling that defines human memory and storytelling. In this sense, Hyperbole and a Half is less a memoir than an epistemological experiment: an inquiry into how we negotiate truth when lived reality exceeds narrative form.
